Saving together.

Hephzibah VSLA is a 30-member village savings and loan association in Gulu City. Every shilling in our loan fund comes from our own members — and every year, it goes back to them, with growth.

Annual share-out

Three cycles. Three share-outs.
Growing every year.

At the end of each annual cycle, all loans are repaid and the entire loan fund — savings plus earnings — is shared out to members in proportion to what they saved. Nothing stays behind but the group's momentum.

Our members

Thirty savers.
One association.

Hephzibah is women-led and open to all. Our members elect their own management committee, write their own constitution, and make every transaction in front of the full group — with the cash box locked behind three keys between meetings.

Beyond the meeting circle

Each of our 30 members comes from a different household, with an average of seven people per home. The savings, loans and share-outs that move through Hephzibah support school fees, medical care, food and small investments across more than 210 people in our community.

Our Social Fund also stands ready with emergency grants when a member's family faces illness, loss or hardship.

Giving back

Growing the movement beyond Hephzibah

What we've learned, we share freely. Hephzibah members volunteer their time and experience so that neighboring communities can enjoy the same benefits of saving together.

Free peer learning

We host open peer-learning sessions for neighboring communities — demonstrating how a VSLA works, sharing our results, and encouraging others to form or join savings groups of their own.

Open to all

Mentoring newer VSLAs

Newly formed savings groups in our area receive hands-on mentorship from Hephzibah — from writing a constitution and electing leaders to running disciplined, transparent meetings.

Ongoing
Group enterprises

Savings that work between meetings

In 2025 we moved beyond lending alone. The group now runs two enterprises whose proceeds flow back into the loan fund — growing what every member takes home at share-out.

Poultry

Group-managed poultry rearing supplies eggs and birds to the local market, turning idle funds into steady group income between lending cycles.

Started 2025

Crop cultivation

Collective farming puts members' agricultural skill to work. Sales of farm produce add a second income stream to the association's earnings.

Started 2025
0 / 30

Twenty-four members now run their own individual businesses — started and grown with loans from the group and proceeds from our shared enterprises. From market stalls to farming ventures, Hephzibah capital is working across Kanyagoga and beyond.

How we work

The VSLA way

We follow the Village Savings and Loan Association methodology — member-owned, member-managed, and fully transparent.

SAVE

Weekly shares

Every member buys 1–5 shares at each meeting, building the loan fund from our own pockets.

BORROW

Member loans

Members borrow up to three times their savings, repayable within three months.

PROTECT

Social Fund

Small regular contributions provide emergency grants when members face hardship.

SHARE

Annual share-out

At year's end, all savings plus earnings are paid back to members in proportion to their shares.

Support our cause

Partner with Hephzibah

Every shilling in our loan fund comes from our members — but well-wishers and partners can help us go further. Your support strengthens what a community has built for itself.

  • Boost our Social Fund for member emergencies
  • Grow our poultry and crop enterprises
  • Equip peer-learning visits to neighboring communities
  • Provide kits (cash boxes, passbooks) for newer VSLAs we mentor
